verdict.rationale: Temporal's docs say failed Activities are retried automatically by default, governed by a configurable Retry Policy. They also say the platform takes over failure handling so developers write less code, and a hands-on user confirms you can retry any unit and specify non-retryable errors. However, the evidence never explicitly shows backoff settings or per-step timeout configuration. missing for 10: explicit documentation of configurable backoff coefficients/intervals, configurable Activity timeouts, independent corroboration of the timeout/backoff behavior

support.subject: As a backend developer, every step retries automatically with configurable backoff, timeouts, and failure policies — no try/catch scaffolding

citations.quote: Temporal's default behavior is to automatically retry an Activity that fails, so transient or intermittent failures require no action on your part.
A Retry Policy is a collection of settings that tells Temporal how and when to try again after something fails
By shifting the burden of failure handling from the application to the platform, there is less code for application developers to write, test, an
You can retry any unit easily on failure and specify non-retryable errors.
